Friday 30 October 2026 · 24 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 1.05% to 22,937 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.91% weighted by turnover, against +0.43% for the median stock, a gap of 2.5 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

V-Guard Industries Limited rose 7.9% on 71 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “V-Guard Industries Limited has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026.”.

BIRLASOFT LIMITED rose 11.9% on 58 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India Limited rose 4.4% on 133 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India Limited has submitted to the Exchange, the Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026.”.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in JSW Dulux Limited (68x), Ramky Infrastructure Limited (60x), DCM Shriram Industries Limited (46x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

What happened
Breaking
Wall Street ends lower as Alphabet revenue miss revives AI capex jitters
Alphabet reported a quarterly revenue shortfall alongside elevated capital expenditure on artificial intelligence infrastructure. For Indian equities, unremunerative AI investments by US tech giants threaten discretionary enterprise IT spending. This pressures revenue growth and order inflows for Indian IT services exporters like TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech.
Reuters Business · +2 others
Warsh shakes up Fed's approach to setting interest rates - KVII
Former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh proposed restructuring the Federal Reserve policy framework to benchmark interest rates against productivity growth rather than headline inflation. A structural shift toward higher terminal US policy rates increases US Treasury yields and strengthens the dollar. This framework change reduces foreign portfolio flows to emerging market equities and weakens the rupee.
Fed and rates
US Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady - GK Today
The Federal Reserve held benchmark interest rates unchanged, citing balanced risks between inflation and employment mandates. Stable US rates preserve the yield differential with Indian debt, supporting foreign fund inflows into domestic equities and stabilizing the rupee. This monetary pause gives the Reserve Bank of India room to maintain domestic repo rates without currency depreciation risk.
Fed and rates
Connected to your data
US inflation heats up in September; consumer spending rises
The US Personal Consumption Expenditures price index increased 0.5% sequentially in September, led by higher energy costs. Accelerated inflation reduces the likelihood of near-term Federal Reserve rate cuts, pushing US Treasury yields higher. Stronger dollar yields trigger foreign portfolio outflows from Indian equities and increase landed crude oil costs for domestic refiners.
ET Markets
Birlasoft share price rallies 11% on huge volume post Q2 results
Birlasoft reported higher quarterly operating margins despite absorbing full-quarter wage hikes and elevated investments in domain capabilities. Operational efficiency and revenue execution offset employee cost expansion, demonstrating cost resilience in mid-tier technology firms. The results indicate stable margin trajectories for mid-cap IT peers such as Coforge and Persistent Systems.
BS Markets
Your themes
Alphabet’s AI risks deepen as filing reveals $98 billion in commitments beyond the $1 trillion spending
Alphabet disclosed $98.5 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments, including data center leases and hardware repurchases, alongside its long-term spending plans. Escalating fixed commitments for AI infrastructure constrain balance sheet flexibility for US tech giants, threatening vendor budgets. This capital reallocation slows cloud migration and outsourced engineering spending for Indian IT services exporters.
AI & data centresET Markets
Intel shares plunge 21% as weak PC demand and supply shortages hit revenue outlook
Intel shares dropped 21% after cutting revenue guidance due to sluggish personal computer demand and manufacturing constraints. The slowdown in traditional enterprise compute spending dampens product engineering demand for Indian ER&D service providers such as L&T Technology Services and Tata Elxsi. Watch Intel's capital expenditure guidance next quarter to assess whether hardware suppliers and system integrators face prolonged order deferrals.
AI & data centresHindu BusinessLine
Nuclear Power Is Back, But Only a Few Stocks Have Customers Signed - The Globe and Mail
Global small modular reactor developers face commercialization delays, with very few firms securing binding power purchase agreements despite surging interest. For Indian equities, this underlines that near-term nuclear revenues remain strictly tied to domestic tenders from state-owned NPCIL rather than export opportunities. Equipment suppliers MTAR Technologies, BHEL, and Larsen & Toubro depend entirely on domestic reactor component orders rather than global licensing timelines.
NuclearNuclear and SMR
India BESS Tender Prices 2026: Winning Bids, Developers, Tariffs and Major Battery Storage Projects - GreentechLead
Recent Indian standalone battery energy storage tenders have cleared at record-low capacity tariffs, supported by viability gap funding and declining global cell prices. Cheaper storage tariffs improve project internal rates of return for renewable developers like Tata Power and JSW Energy bidding for round-the-clock power. However, reliance on imported lithium cells limits margin expansion for domestic battery manufacturers such as Amara Raja and Exide.
Green energy & solarGeopolitics
Suzlon Energy Q2 Results: Profit plunges 69% YoY to Rs 394 crore due to one-time deferred tax
Suzlon Energy reported a 69% year-on-year drop in Q2 net profit to 394 crore rupees, driven by a one-time deferred tax adjustment. Core operations remained solid, with revenue growing 26% to 4,869 crore rupees and delivery volumes expanding. A 6,009 MW order book and 2,048 crore rupees in net cash shield execution margins from working-capital interest costs across upcoming quarters.
InfrastructureET Markets
Capital markets
Engie looks to expand India presence with renewable and battery development
French utility Engie plans to expand its Indian renewable and battery storage capacity, joining a growing pool of foreign-backed independent power producers. Heightened competitive intensity in upcoming solar and storage auctions will likely keep tariff realizations low, compressing generation margins for incumbents NTPC Green and Tata Power. Conversely, capital deployment by foreign developers supports order intake for domestic equipment suppliers and balance-of-plant contractors.
Reuters Business
Polymarket resumes trading after third-party security breach, to reimburse users
This offshore prediction platform breach has no transmission channel to Indian listed equities, domestic liquidity or currency markets.
Reuters Business
Finmin pegs Q2 expansion at 7.35%,flags capital pressure over US yield
The Finance Ministry estimates September-quarter growth at 7.35%, driven by manufacturing and tax collections, while warning that elevated US Treasury yields threaten foreign capital inflows. Resilient domestic activity supports bank credit growth and capital goods order execution. Elevated US yields compress sovereign spreads, keeping foreign portfolio flows defensive and pressuring the rupee until official NSO data confirms the growth trajectory late this month.
ET Economy
Macro and economy
Amazon shares fall 6% as $77 billion AI spending raises cash flow concerns
Amazon projected annual capital expenditure of $75 billion to expand cloud computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure. Rising hyperscaler infrastructure investment supports Indian IT service providers handling cloud migrations and enterprise workload deployments, including Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys. Persistently cautious retail demand signals that broad enterprise IT budgets remain tight, with upcoming client quarterly commentary required to confirm any recovery in discretionary software spending.
Hindu BusinessLine
responsAbility invests $20 million in Navitas Solar as part of its Asia Climate Fund: What is it?
Swiss asset manager responsAbility invested $20 million in unlisted manufacturer Navitas Solar to expand module production. The funding expands domestic manufacturing capacity behind tariff protections, increasing domestic competition for listed equipment peers like Premier Energies and Waaree Energies. Capacity expansion execution timelines across Indian solar fabricators will determine whether domestic module prices face downward pressure over the next two quarters.

Companies and earnings
Samsung keeps shattering profit records as AI boom lifts chip demand
Global memory chip demand driven by high-bandwidth AI hardware drove Samsung to record earnings. Sustained server capex by hyperscalers supports Indian tier-one IT services providers through enterprise cloud and data architecture contracts. Sustained deal momentum depends on US enterprise software budgets holding up in upcoming fourth-quarter corporate guidance.
BS Markets
India’s cloud data capacity projected to grow nearly 4-5 times by 2030: Govt factsheet - The Hans India
A government factsheet projects India's cloud data centre capacity will expand four to five times by 2030, driven by digital data localisation and AI workloads. This capital expenditure drives long-term power demand and order books for industrial electrical equipment makers Schneider Electric Infrastructure and Hitachi Energy. Captive renewable power tariffs will determine operational returns for operators.
Data centres and AI capex
Mondelez tops third-quarter profit estimates on easing cost pressures
Mondelez beat third-quarter profit estimates as cocoa and packaging inflation softened against resilient selling prices. Easing raw material inflation supports gross margins for domestic confectioners and packaged food players like Nestle India and Britannia Industries. Forthcoming quarterly gross margin prints will confirm whether Indian operations retain these input savings or pass them into promotional discounts.
Reuters Business
Hero MotoCorp bets on premiumisation, EVs to sustain growth momentum
Hero MotoCorp expanded its scooter and Vida electric vehicle volumes in the September quarter, lifting its segment market share to 7.3 percent. Margin expansion hinges on this product mix shift, as higher realizations on premium motorcycles offset lower gross margins from electric models. Market share data in the 125cc-plus motorcycle category will confirm whether operating margins can approach 14 percent.
ET Markets
Geopolitics
India says trade deal with US will not hurt its farmers
The commerce ministry confirmed that ongoing bilateral trade discussions with the United States will protect domestic agricultural import tariffs. Excluding farm products insulates listed agrochemical suppliers and seed producers like PI Industries and Kaveri Seed from lower-cost grain imports. This policy continuity preserves domestic crop pricing power while trade negotiations focus on manufacturing and technology services.
Reuters Business · +1 other
Russia to extend diesel export ban, use quotas to fulfil US deal, sources say
Russia plans to extend its diesel export restrictions and manage external volumes through state-allocated quotas. Tightening seaborne middle distillate supplies supports regional refining cracks, directly lifting gross refining margins for Indian fuel exporters Reliance Industries and Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals. Weekly Singapore gasoil crack spreads will indicate the immediate margin gain for domestic refiners.
Reuters Business
COMMENTARY: Warsh's muddled messaging revives Fed credibility doubts - Reuters
Kevin Warsh's conflicting policy stances favoring rate cuts while aggressively shrinking the Federal Reserve's balance sheet have raised doubts over future US monetary direction. Unpredictable US rate paths drive dollar volatility, curbing foreign portfolio flows into Indian equities and narrowing the Reserve Bank of India's headroom to cut policy rates. That directly caps valuation multiples for domestic rate-sensitive financials, real estate, and auto stocks.
